full_judgment: 2. The petitioner filed an application on 27.9.1973 praying for settlement of the disputed land measuring .10 decimals appertaining to plot No. 759 contiguous to the homestead of the petitioner. Upon receiving the application, an inquiry was held by the local Tahshilder who submitted report with findings that the land is Government Khas land and fit for cultivation and recommended for settlement of the land. The Circle Officer (Revenue), on receipt of the said report after hearing the petitioner and on perusal of the report and S.A. Khatian, rejected the prayer. The petitioner filed an application for review against the said order before the Circle Officer (Revenue) who sent the application to the Surveyor for physical verification to ascertain whether the land for which settlement was proposed is under Cultivation and possession of the applicant. The surveyor, after verification, submitted his report with a sketch map showing that .10 decimals land out of total land .73 decimals was in Possession of the applicant who has been cultivating the same and it was not required by the public as Rasta. Thereafter, by notice, objection from the public was invited, but as no objection was filed, the Circle Officer (Revenue), on perusal of the report of the Surveyor and other papers, found that the petitioner was the most' deserving candidate for lease of the land and sent a proposal for settlement of the same to the Sub-Divisional Officer, Sadar, Comilla, who accepted the proposal and granted lease. The petitioner executed a Kabuliyat on payment of Salami in favour of the Government and a Khatian was opened in his name in respect of the said land as tenant and he has been enjoying the land since then under Government. While the petitioner has possessed the land, one Fariduddin, an employee of the Comilla Collectorate, threatened him to dispossess from the said land. He also filed a petition before Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Comilla, in August, 1978, praying for settlement of the suit land in favour, of his brother. The Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Comilla without any lawful authority treated the same as an appeal and started the settlement case and directed the Circle Officer (Revenue) to submit report on enquiry. On enquiry, the Circle Officer (Revenue) submitted the report against the settlement in favour of the petitioner to which the petitioner filed written objection before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Comilla. But the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Comilla, by an ex-parte order dated 26.6.1979; cancelled the lease granted in favour of petitioner. The petitioner thereafter filed a review petition before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) in vain leading to institution of the Title suit No. 483 of 1979 in the Court of Munsif, Comilla, for declaration that order of the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) cancelling the lease without any lawful authority on the allegation, inter alia, that the disputed land is the Government Khas land and the same was not "gopath", was under cultivation of his predecissor and thereafter under his cultivation and that was not required for the use of the public as pathway.
